title: Answer critics openly, for their weapons will not prosper
setting: Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon were revising the Bible at the John Johnson home in Hiram, Ohio. Ezra Booth, a former member, had published critical letters in the Ohio Star of Ravenna since October 1831. Symonds Rider, also disaffected, had given a February 1831 revelation to another local paper. On 1 December 1831, Joseph dictated this revelation, which set the Bible work aside so both men could preach. Rigdon later challenged both critics to public meetings, and both declined.
summary: The revelation tells Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon that the time has come to preach. They are to expound the scriptures by the Spirit given them. They are to preach in the nearby regions and in the church for a season. This work will prepare the way for revelations still to come. They are to invite their enemies to meet them in public and in private. If they are faithful, their critics’ shame will be shown. The revelation promises that no weapon formed against them will prosper. It closes by telling them to keep the commandments.

contextNote.title: A promise given with an assignment
contextNote.text: Critics were attacking the church in nearby newspapers. Verse 7 tells Joseph and Sidney to answer by calling their enemies to meet them openly. Verse 8 even invites the critics to bring their “strong reasons” against the Lord. Verse 9 gives the ground for this confidence: no weapon formed against them will prosper. Verse 10 adds that opponents will be confounded “in mine own due time,” not at once. Here the promise does not remove opposition; it backs an open, faithful reply to it.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 71–75 takes its title, “No Weapon That Is Formed against You Shall Prosper,” from verse 9. According to verses 4 and 7, what were Joseph and Sidney to do instead of staying silent?
reviewNote: Read all 11 verses. Official heading gives Hiram, 1 December 1831, Bible translation laid aside, and Ezra Booth’s letters. JSP adds Symonds Rider (JSP spelling), the Ohio Star in Ravenna, the Johnson home, and Rigdon’s challenges, which both men declined. Booth and Rider are not named in the text, so they are not in personIds; Ravenna is not in the gazetteer and is not named in the text. Fact-check 2026-10-12: setting said Rider gave the revelation to "another Ravenna paper"; JSP says only another local paper and identifies it as a February 1831 revelation.
